panels.title: Payment decision throughput, by outcome
panels.description: atlas_payments_decisions_total — the only place a rejection is visible at all, since DECISION 1 returns every rejection on HTTP 200. A status-code panel here would show a healthy service through an outage; this is the panel that actually would not.

panels.title: Fraud assessment source — MODEL vs FALLBACK_RULES
panels.description: A spike in FALLBACK_RULES is the signal the fraud service (or the circuit breaker protecting the call to it) is down — see RestFraudClient and ConservativeRuleFallback. This panel is the operational answer to 'is the fraud model actually running right now'.

panels.title: Flagged rate (last 15m)
panels.description: or vector(0) on the numerator: Prometheus returns an empty result (not zero) for a label combination that has never occurred, e.g. flagged="true" before any payment has ever been flagged - without the fallback this panel would show 'No data' instead of the more honest 0%.

panels.title: POST /payments latency — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Server-side processing time, via Prometheus's own histogram_quantile() over http_server_requests_seconds — computed here because Micrometer's client-side percentiles cannot be correctly aggregated across instances the way histogram buckets can (see application.yaml's percentiles-histogram setting). This is a different measurement point from k6's client-observed round trip in the README's load-test table; the two are not expected to match exactly.

panels.title: Circuit breaker state — fraud-service
panels.description: resilience4j_circuitbreaker_state — 0/1 per state label. A 1 on the 'open' series means every payment is currently on the conservative rule fallback, not the model.
